*This page is a benchmark of the method. To use repdist on your own data, start with [Get started](vignette.html).*

In plain terms: KEGG's ko-rn table lists, for each metabolic reaction, every
KO (KEGG Orthology group) known to catalyse it. When a reaction has two or
more KOs, those KOs are alternative enzymes for the same step: interchangeable
by function, not required to share a fold. One simulated condition is
enriched for every protein of one such reaction's KOs, pooled; the other is
not. Unlike [Simulation 2](simulation_ec.html)'s EC3 classes, which can group
structurally unrelated, convergent enzymes, a KO is itself already a
fine-grained orthology call; the question here is whether the proteins of
several *different* KOs that share one reaction behave as one functional
unit under `repdist`, and whether that beats counting KOs directly.

**Question.** Can a TM-Vec similarity graph -- with or without the homology
(E-value) gate -- group proteins of several KOs that KEGG assigns to one
shared reaction, and support differential abundance and MMD, relative to a
naive "count by KO" baseline that already knows the KO labels?

```{r libs}
library(repdist)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
```

# Data and provenance

**Data.** The input file is `curated/simulation_kofam.rds`, built by
`data-raw/simulation_kofam.R` from KEGG REST (ko-rn, BRITE ko00001; KEGG is
copyright Kanehisa Laboratories, not open-licensed
[@kanehisa2000kegg]) and UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot [@uniprot2025] (CC BY 4.0). See
`data-raw/README.md` and `KOFAM_SIM_PLAN.md` for the selection algorithm
(KO-reaction grouping, the subunit/homology/leakage filters, and the open
licensing question for a public KO-labelled build, `KOFAM_SIM_PLAN.md`
section 11).

```{r data}
kofam_path <- file.path("curated", "simulation_kofam.rds")
```

# Count model

The same negative-binomial model as
[Simulation 1](simulation_funfam.html#count-model) and
[Simulation 2](simulation_ec.html#count-model), with depth $D = 2 \times
10^4$, size factor $s_i \sim \mathrm{LogNormal}(0, 0.25)$ and dispersion
$\phi_{ij} = (0.1 + 1/\mu_{ij})\, e_j$, $e_j \sim \mathrm{LogNormal}(0, 0.5)$,
but restructured for this page's design (`KOFAM_SIM_PLAN.md` section 6): every
sample of condition A puts a share $\rho$ of its expected abundance evenly
over *every* treatment-reaction protein (pooled across its KOs), and
condition B has $\rho = 0$, an asymmetric enrichment-versus-null design
rather than the symmetric per-sample single-protein enrichment of
Simulations 1-2. `nb_counts()` there loops per sample and per-sample
enrichment set; here the enrichment set is the same for every sample of
condition A, so the loop collapses to one group-level update.

```{r count-model}
depth <- 2e4
nb_counts_kofam <- function(ids, group, rho, enrich_set, levels_ab = c("A", "B")) {
    n <- length(group)
    pi <- setNames(rlnorm(length(ids)), ids)
    pi <- pi / sum(pi)
    s <- rlnorm(n, 0, 0.25)
    e <- rlnorm(length(ids), 0, 0.5)
    p <- matrix(pi, n, length(ids), byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(names(group), ids))
    is_a <- group == levels_ab[1]
    p[is_a, ] <- (1 - rho) * p[is_a, ]
    p[is_a, enrich_set] <- p[is_a, enrich_set] + rho / length(enrich_set)
    mu <- s * depth * p
    phi <- (0.1 + 1 / mu) * rep(e, each = n)
    matrix(rnbinom(length(mu), mu = mu, size = 1 / phi), n, dimnames = dimnames(p))
}
```

$\rho \in \{0, 1\%, 2\%, 5\%\}$; $\rho = 0$ is the global null (Section 6).
Sample size per condition $n \in \{10, 20\}$ (`KOFAM_SIM_PLAN.md`'s planning
caps); `r if (isTRUE(smoke)) "the smoke build uses n = 4 and 2 replicates" else "the full grid uses 50 replicates per (rho, n)"`.

```{r design, eval = have_kofam}
rhos <- c(0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05)
n_grid <- if (isTRUE(smoke)) 4L else c(10L, 20L)
n_rep <- if (isTRUE(smoke)) 2L else 50L
treatment_proteins <- ann$protein[ann$role == "treatment"]
simulate_kofam <- function(seed, rho, n_per_group) {
    set.seed(seed)
    group <- factor(rep(c("A", "B"), each = n_per_group), c("A", "B"))
    names(group) <- sprintf("s%02d", seq_along(group))
    counts <- nb_counts_kofam(ann$protein, group, rho, treatment_proteins)
    list(counts = counts, group = group)
}
```

# Method variants

All four variants start from the same universe and, for the three graph
variants, the same `protein_similarity()` call, so differences are not
confounded by re-alignment (`KOFAM_SIM_PLAN.md` section 7):

1. **Combined** (package default): `max_evalue = 0.01`, edge weight = TM-Vec
   cosine, `bin_proteins()`.
2. **Embedding only**: `max_evalue = Inf` (no homology gate), same cosine
   weights, `bin_proteins()`.
3. **Homology only**: the combined graph's support (E $\le$ 0.01 edges),
   reweighted to 1 (unweighted), because `bin_proteins()` requires a
   similarity in $[0, 1]$ and the package discards bit scores. The optional
   bit-score sensitivity of `KOFAM_SIM_PLAN.md` section 7 needs cached
   alignments and is not computed here (see `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md`).
4. **Naive KO baseline**: counts summed by the protein's own KO annotation
   (already known, no embedding), tested the same way as the bin-level
   variants. This is the "just count KOs" comparator.

```{r bins, eval = have_kofam}
n_cores <- BiocParallel::multicoreWorkers()
S_combined <- protein_similarity(kofam_proteins, n_cores = n_cores)
S_embed <- protein_similarity(kofam_proteins, max_evalue = Inf)
S_homology <- matrix(0, nrow(S_combined), ncol(S_combined), dimnames = dimnames(S_combined))
S_homology[S_combined > 0] <- 1
diag(S_homology) <- 1
graphs <- list(combined = S_combined, `embedding only` = S_embed,
    `homology only` = S_homology)
bins <- lapply(graphs, bin_proteins)
ko_of <- setNames(ann$ko, ann$protein)
glom_ko <- function(counts) t(rowsum(t(counts), ko_of[colnames(counts)]))
```

# Differential abundance

Raw counts are summed within each bin (or KO, for the naive baseline) with
`bin_glom()` and tested with DESeq2 [@love2014deseq2], as in the
[case study](case_study.html#differential-abundance): design `~ group`,
`poscounts` size factors, Wald test, contrast A vs B. A unit is called at
adjusted p $\le$ 0.05. It is a true positive only if a majority of its
total abundance in that replicate's counts comes from treatment-reaction
proteins (a purity rule, recorded here, not tuned on the result); an
empirical FDR is the share of calls that fail this rule.

```{r da-helper, eval = have_kofam}
da_call <- function(agg_counts, group) {
    keep <- colSums(agg_counts) > 0
    dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(round(t(agg_counts[, keep, drop = FALSE])),
        data.frame(group = group), ~ group)
    # The parametric and "mean" dispersion fits can both fail on a small
    # KOFAM_SMOKE universe (tens of proteins, few bins), with DESeq2's
    # own message that gene-wise estimates should be used as the final
    # dispersions. Rebuild the DESeqDataSet inside each attempt so a
    # failed fit does not leave a half-modified object.
    fit <- function(fitType = NULL) {
        d <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(round(t(agg_counts[, keep, drop = FALSE])),
            data.frame(group = group), ~ group)
        if (is.null(fitType)) {
            DESeq2::DESeq(d, sfType = "poscounts", quiet = TRUE)
        } else {
            DESeq2::DESeq(d, sfType = "poscounts", fitType = fitType, quiet = TRUE)
        }
    }
    gene_wise <- function() {
        d <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(round(t(agg_counts[, keep, drop = FALSE])),
            data.frame(group = group), ~ group)
        d <- DESeq2::estimateSizeFactors(d, type = "poscounts")
        d <- DESeq2::estimateDispersionsGeneEst(d)
        DESeq2::dispersions(d) <- S4Vectors::mcols(d)$dispGeneEst
        DESeq2::nbinomWaldTest(d, quiet = TRUE)
    }
    dds <- tryCatch(fit(),
        error = function(e) tryCatch(fit("mean"), error = function(e2) gene_wise()))
    res <- as.data.frame(DESeq2::results(dds, contrast = c("group", "A", "B"), alpha = 0.05))
    res$unit <- colnames(agg_counts)[keep]
    res
}
is_treatment <- setNames(ann$role == "treatment", ann$protein)
# Share of a unit's (bin's or KO's) total abundance in this replicate's
# counts that sits on treatment-reaction proteins, from the protein-level
# counts and a protein -> unit membership (not the aggregated counts, which
# no longer distinguish treatment from background proteins within a unit).
purity <- function(counts, membership) {
    ids <- colnames(counts)
    tot <- colSums(counts)
    treat <- tot * is_treatment[ids]
    unit <- membership[ids]
    tapply(treat, unit, sum) / tapply(tot, unit, sum)
}
da_one_replicate <- function(sim) {
    membership <- lapply(bins, function(b) b$membership)
    membership$`naive KO` <- ko_of
    agg <- list(
        combined = bin_glom(sim$counts, bins$combined),
        `embedding only` = bin_glom(sim$counts, bins$`embedding only`),
        `homology only` = bin_glom(sim$counts, bins$`homology only`),
        `naive KO` = glom_ko(sim$counts)
    )
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(agg), function(m) {
        res <- da_call(agg[[m]], sim$group)
        share <- purity(sim$counts, membership[[m]])
        res$treatment_share <- share[res$unit]
        res$method <- m
        res
    }))
}
```

## Representative replicate

$\rho$ = 2%, fixed before any result (the same value used in Simulations 1-2,
chosen there from the case study's glycoside hydrolase enrichment
[@blakeleyruiz2025diet]).

```{r kofam-example, eval = have_kofam}
sim <- simulate_kofam(1, 0.02, n_grid[1])
res <- da_one_replicate(sim)
called <- res[!is.na(res$padj) & res$padj <= 0.05, ]
tp <- called$treatment_share > 0.5
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(split(res, res$method), function(d) {
    c(units = nrow(d),
        called = sum(!is.na(d$padj) & d$padj <= 0.05),
        `true positive` = sum(tp[res$method[!is.na(res$padj) & res$padj <= 0.05] == d$method[1]]))
})), caption = "Units called at adjusted p <= 0.05 and the true positives among them")
```

## All replicates

Repeated at every $\rho$, `r if (isTRUE(smoke)) "the smoke n_rep (2)" else "n_rep = 50"`
times, with the same seed at every $\rho$ for one replicate. Power is the
share of replicates with at least one true-positive call; empirical FDR is
the share of calls (at $\rho > 0$) that are not true positives. The $\rho =
0$ column is the Type I sanity check.

```{r kofam-benchmark, eval = have_kofam}
bench <- do.call(rbind, lapply(n_grid, function(n_per_group) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(rhos, function(rho) {
        do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_rep), function(r) {
            sim <- simulate_kofam(r, rho, n_per_group)
            res <- da_one_replicate(sim)
            data.frame(n = n_per_group, rho = rho, replicate = r, res,
                row.names = NULL)
        }))
    }))
}))
bench$called <- !is.na(bench$padj) & bench$padj <= 0.05
bench$tp <- bench$called & bench$treatment_share > 0.5
summ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(bench, list(bench$method, bench$n, bench$rho)), function(d) {
    if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
    power <- mean(tapply(d$tp, d$replicate, any))
    fdr <- if (sum(d$called)) mean(!d$tp[d$called]) else NA_real_
    data.frame(method = d$method[1], n = d$n[1], rho = d$rho[1],
        power = power, FDR = fdr)
}))
knitr::kable(summ[order(summ$method, summ$n, summ$rho), ], digits = 3,
    row.names = FALSE)
```

# MMD

`sample_mmd()`, the maximum mean discrepancy between samples under a
Gaussian kernel on the embeddings [@gretton2012mmd], on the same relative
abundances, plus PERMANOVA [@anderson2001permanova; @oksanen2025vegan] on
the representative replicate and across the grid (999 permutations).

```{r kofam-mmd, eval = have_kofam}
mmd_test <- function(sim) {
    D <- sample_mmd(sim$counts / rowSums(sim$counts), kofam_proteins)
    set.seed(1)
    a <- vegan::adonis2(D ~ group, data = data.frame(group = sim$group), permutations = 999)
    c(R2 = a$R2[1], p = a$`Pr(>F)`[1])
}
mmd_bench <- do.call(rbind, lapply(n_grid, function(n_per_group) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(rhos, function(rho) {
        r <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_rep), function(rep_i) {
            mmd_test(simulate_kofam(rep_i, rho, n_per_group))
        }))
        data.frame(n = n_per_group, rho = rho, `power (p<=0.05)` = mean(r[, "p"] <= 0.05),
            `median R2` = median(r[, "R2"]), check.names = FALSE)
    }))
}))
knitr::kable(mmd_bench, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Protein clustering against the KO labels

The MCL bins depend only on the universe and its graph, not on any
simulated counts, so they are scored once per method against two labellings
of `r if (have_kofam) length(kofam_proteins)` proteins: the two-way label
(treatment-reaction vs background) and the fine-grained KO label. Score is
the pairwise similarity (cosine for the combined/embedding graphs, 0/1 for
the unweighted homology graph) as a predictor of "both proteins are
treatment-reaction members"; AUPRC is from `PRROC::pr.curve()`. ARI and NMI compare the MCL bins to each
labelling with `aricode`.

```{r kofam-clustering, eval = have_kofam}
two_way <- setNames(ifelse(ann$role == "treatment", "treatment", "background"), ann$protein)
clust_metrics <- function(S, bin) {
    ids <- rownames(S)
    pos <- outer(two_way[ids] == "treatment", two_way[ids] == "treatment", "&")
    score <- S[upper.tri(S)]
    label <- pos[upper.tri(pos)]
    pr <- PRROC::pr.curve(scores.class0 = score[label], scores.class1 = score[!label],
        curve = FALSE)
    # aricode::ARI/NMI coerce labels with as.numeric(); character labels
    # such as "bin1" or "treatment" become NA. Map to integer codes first.
    codes <- function(x) as.integer(factor(x))
    c(AUPRC = pr$auc.integral,
        `ARI (2-way)` = aricode::ARI(codes(bin$membership[ids]), codes(two_way[ids])),
        `NMI (2-way)` = aricode::NMI(codes(bin$membership[ids]), codes(two_way[ids])),
        `ARI (KO)` = aricode::ARI(codes(bin$membership[ids]), codes(ko_of[ids])),
        `NMI (KO)` = aricode::NMI(codes(bin$membership[ids]), codes(ko_of[ids])))
}
clust_scores <- t(mapply(clust_metrics, graphs, bins))
knitr::kable(clust_scores, digits = 3)
```

# Summary

```{r summary-values, include = FALSE}
if (have_kofam) {
    pw <- function(m, rho_val, n_val) {
        summ$power[summ$method == m & summ$rho == rho_val & summ$n == n_val]
    }
    n1 <- n_grid[1]
}
```

- **Treatment group.** `r if (have_kofam) treatment_reaction else "(no build)"`
  with `r if (have_kofam) length(unique(ann$ko[ann$role == 'treatment'])) else NA`
  KOs passed the subunit-language screen, the minimum-proteins-per-KO rule
  and the cross-KO homology/leakage check.
- **Differential abundance.** At $\rho$ = 2%, $n$ = `r if (have_kofam) n1 else NA`,
  power was `r if (have_kofam) sprintf('%.2f', pw("combined", 0.02, n1)) else "NA"`
  for the combined graph's bins,
  `r if (have_kofam) sprintf('%.2f', pw("homology only", 0.02, n1)) else "NA"`
  for homology-only bins and
  `r if (have_kofam) sprintf('%.2f', pw("naive KO", 0.02, n1)) else "NA"`
  for the naive KO baseline, against a Type I rate ($\rho$ = 0) of
  `r if (have_kofam) sprintf('%.2f', pw("combined", 0, n1)) else "NA"`,
  `r if (have_kofam) sprintf('%.2f', pw("homology only", 0, n1)) else "NA"` and
  `r if (have_kofam) sprintf('%.2f', pw("naive KO", 0, n1)) else "NA"`
  respectively.
- **Clustering.** `r if (have_kofam) "See the AUPRC/ARI/NMI table above for how each graph's pairwise similarity and MCL bins track the treatment-reaction label and the finer KO label." else "(no build)"`

`r if (isTRUE(smoke)) "This page's object is a KOFAM_SMOKE=1 pipeline check (random embeddings, tens of proteins); none of the numbers above are a result." else ""`

The naive KO baseline already knows every protein's KO, so it is a strong
comparator whenever KO annotation is complete; the open question this page
asks is whether the embedding graph's bins recover the same reaction-level
unit *without* being told the KO labels, and whether MMD detects the
contrast at all. [MCL parameters](parameters.html) and
[Simulation 2](simulation_ec.html) discuss the same bins under enzyme-class
and threshold questions.
